title: Cost of the Fourier estimator program
statement: Let $m$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let the sample be a map from an $m$-element index set to binary vectors of length $n$, and let $U$ be a finite set of coordinates. Running the small-bias Fourier estimator program with oracle $f$ returns the sample average of $f(x)$ times the monomial indexed by $U$, where each binary sample is converted to a sign vector, together with its prescribed cost: zero random examples, $m$ membership queries, and $m(|U|+2)+1$ units of local work.
hypotheses_covered: real-valued function on the n-dimensional sign cube
sample of m binary vectors of length n
